Real World Example: Service item or handmade item
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has no stock entries at all.
Current App Behavior: System skips stock modal and sells using base product price with no selected stock.
Question For PM: Should stock-enabled items with no stock rows still be sellable?
Suggested Default: Allow base-price sale and leave stock_id empty.

Real World Example: Bakery item sold out but still sellable manually
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has stock rows, but all quantities are 0.
Current App Behavior: Selectable stock list becomes empty. System falls back to base product price and sells without selected stock.
Question For PM: When all stock rows are 0, should sale continue on base price or be blocked?
Suggested Default: Allow base-price sale.

Real World Example: Bad stock data import
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has stock rows, but all quantities are null or negative.
Current App Behavior: Rows are not selectable because only qty > 0 is treated as available. System falls back to base product price.
Question For PM: Should null or negative stock be treated the same as 0 stock, or should item be blocked for data cleanup?
Suggested Default: Treat as unavailable stock and allow base-price sale only if business wants permissive selling.

Real World Example: Mixed stock ledger
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has some rows with qty > 0 and some rows with qty 0 or null.
Current App Behavior: Only positive-quantity rows are considered. Zero or null rows never appear for selection.
Question For PM: Should zero or null quantity rows stay hidden, or should cashier see them as informational rows?
Suggested Default: Hide non-sellable rows from selection.

Real World Example: Single batch medicine
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has exactly one stock row with qty > 0 in the active store.
Current App Behavior: No modal is shown. Product is auto-added using that stock's price and MRP.
Question For PM: Is silent auto-selection correct when only one sellable stock row exists?
Suggested Default: Yes, auto-select and add directly.

Real World Example: No store selected yet
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Product has multiple positive stock rows. No active store id and no active store name are available.
Current App Behavior: System does not filter by store and considers all positive stock rows.
Question For PM: If no store context exists, should all positive stock be considered, or should sale be blocked until store is known?
Suggested Default: Require store context only if multi-store accuracy matters; otherwise allow all positive stock.

Real World Example: Multi-store inventory working normally
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Active store id exists. Some positive stock rows match the active store id.
Current App Behavior: System filters by active store id and only matching positive stock rows are considered.
Question For PM: Is strict store-id filtering the correct business rule?
Suggested Default: Yes, use active store id as the primary filter.

Real World Example: Stock exists in another outlet only
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Positive stock exists, but none match the active store.
Current App Behavior: System finds no selectable stock for the active store and falls back to base product price selling.
Question For PM: If another store has stock but the current store does not, should current store still be allowed to sell by base price?
Suggested Default: Usually block or warn, unless cross-store selling without stock lock is allowed.

Real World Example: Store id mismatch but store name matches
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock enabled. Active store id exists, but stock rows match only by store name, not by store id.
Current App Behavior: Current logic uses store id first and does not fall back to name matching when an id exists.
Question For PM: If store id is present but mismatched due to bad data, should the system still fall back to store name matching?
Suggested Default: Prefer strict id match for safety, but confirm if name fallback is needed for dirty data.

Real World Example: Stock feature turned off for simple POS mode
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock disabled globally. Product may still have stock rows in data.
Current App Behavior: System ignores stock selection and uses product base price directly.
Question For PM: When stock is disabled, should stock-specific prices be ignored completely?
Suggested Default: Yes, ignore stock rows when stock feature is off.

Real World Example: Cola cans from two inward entries
Scenario / Preconditions: Two or more positive stock rows have the same sale price, MRP, purchase price, unit, HSN code, and tax rate.
Current App Behavior: System combines rows into one pricing group and sums quantity.
Question For PM: Is this exact grouping rule correct?
Suggested Default: Yes, combine rows only when all pricing-relevant fields match.

Real World Example: Two batches with same selling price but different MRP
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same sale price but different MRP.
Current App Behavior: System keeps them as separate pricing groups and may show the modal.
Question For PM: Should different MRP force separate choices even if sale price is the same?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep separate if MRP matters to cashier or customer.

Real World Example: Old purchase cost and new purchase cost
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same sale price and MRP but different purchase price.
Current App Behavior: System keeps them as separate pricing groups.
Question For PM: Should purchase price differences matter for cashier-side stock selection?
Suggested Default: If only selling behavior matters, consider combining; if margin tracking matters, keep separate.

Real World Example: Loose item vs boxed unit
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same price but different unit.
Current App Behavior: System keeps them as separate pricing groups.
Question For PM: Should different units always be separate even if price is identical?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep separate because quantity interpretation changes.

Real World Example: Same price but different HSN classification
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same price and MRP but different HSN code.
Current App Behavior: System keeps them as separate pricing groups.
Question For PM: Should tax or compliance classification differences always prevent grouping?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep separate if HSN affects billing or reporting.

Real World Example: Same price but different GST/VAT rate
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same price and MRP but different tax rate.
Current App Behavior: System keeps them as separate pricing groups.
Question For PM: Should different tax rates always force separate choices?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep separate.

Real World Example: Dairy item with same price but different expiry
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same pricing fields but different expiry dates.
Current App Behavior: System still combines them because expiry is not part of the grouping key.
Question For PM: Should expiry date affect grouping, or is current no-expiry grouping acceptable?
Suggested Default: If FEFO matters, expiry should affect selection or at least final stock pick.

Real World Example: Same pricing, different inward dates
Scenario / Preconditions: Positive stock rows have same pricing fields but different stock dates.
Current App Behavior: System combines them because stock date is not part of the grouping key.
Question For PM: Should stock date influence grouping or automatic selection?
Suggested Default: Usually no for UI grouping, but yes for deduction order if FIFO is required.

Real World Example: Many raw rows, one sell price
Scenario / Preconditions: Multiple raw stock rows exist, but after grouping there is exactly one pricing group.
Current App Behavior: System skips the modal and auto-selects the single pricing group.
Question For PM: Should the cashier still see a modal for visibility even when only one pricing group exists?
Suggested Default: No modal; auto-add for speed.

Real World Example: Old batch and new batch at different prices
Scenario / Preconditions: Multiple raw stock rows exist, and after grouping there are multiple pricing groups.
Current App Behavior: System opens the multi-stock modal.
Question For PM: Is modal-based manual choice the right UX when multiple pricing groups remain?
Suggested Default: Yes, require explicit choice.

Real World Example: Combined pricing row in stock modal
Scenario / Preconditions: Modal is open and a grouped row is visible.
User Action: Cashier clicks the top-level Choose button on a grouped row.
Current App Behavior: System returns one representative stock row with combined quantity and uses that for cart selection.
Question For PM: Should top-level Choose be allowed, or should cashier be forced to choose an exact underlying stock row?
Suggested Default: Allow top-level Choose only if backend can safely handle grouped deduction.

Real World Example: Cashier wants to inspect grouped rows
Scenario / Preconditions: Modal shows a grouped row with multiple underlying stock entries.
Current App Behavior: System shows the list of individual stock entries under that grouped row.
Question For PM: Is expand-and-inspect enough detail for the cashier, or should more fields be visible up front?
Suggested Default: Keep compact view with optional expand.

Real World Example: Cashier wants exact stock row
Scenario / Preconditions: Modal shows expanded individual stock entries.
User Action: Cashier clicks Choose on one individual stock row.
Current App Behavior: System uses that exact underlying stock row for cart selection.
Question For PM: Should exact-row choosing remain available inside grouped rows?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep exact selection for advanced control.

Real World Example: Cashier changes mind
Scenario / Preconditions: Modal is open.
User Action: Cashier clicks Cancel or closes the modal.
Current App Behavior: Current flow aborts the add-to-cart action completely.
Question For PM: If cashier cancels stock selection, should the item still be added using base price, or should add be cancelled?
Suggested Default: Cancel the add completely.

Real World Example: Sold-out rows in grouped product
Scenario / Preconditions: Product has some stock rows with qty 0 and some with qty > 0.
Current App Behavior: Only positive-quantity rows are represented. Zero-quantity rows never appear.
Question For PM: Should sold-out rows be hidden, or shown as disabled for visibility?
Suggested Default: Hide sold-out rows from modal.

Real World Example: One pricing group, many raw rows
Scenario / Preconditions: Multiple raw stock rows combine into a single pricing group.
Current App Behavior: No stock modal is shown, so cashier never sees a Choose button.
Question For PM: If only one pricing group remains but multiple actual stock rows exist, should the app still auto-add, or should it ask which exact stock to use?
Suggested Default: Auto-add only if FIFO or FEFO deduction is deterministic.

Real World Example: Grouped selection inventory accuracy
Scenario / Preconditions: Cashier picks a grouped row using top-level Choose.
User Action: Order is added to cart and later confirmed.
Current App Behavior: Business flow works, but inventory deduction may be tied to one representative stock id instead of all grouped rows.
Question For PM: Is grouped selection acceptable if inventory tracks against one representative stock, or must exact-row deduction be enforced?
Suggested Default: Require exact-row handling if stock ledger accuracy is critical.

Real World Example: Walk-in customer without pricing history feature
Scenario / Preconditions: Add-to-cart is direct, but customer history setting is off, or no customer id/name is available.
Current App Behavior: System skips purchase-history lookup and uses current stock or base price.
Question For PM: Is it correct to bypass purchase history unless a valid customer and feature flag exist?
Suggested Default: Yes, skip history unless explicitly enabled and customer is known.

Real World Example: Default customer used for generic billing
Scenario / Preconditions: Customer history setting is on, but selected customer is the default customer.
Current App Behavior: System skips purchase-history modal for the default customer.
Question For PM: Should default customer always skip customer-specific price history?
Suggested Default: Yes, skip history for default customer.

Real World Example: Regular customer with no prior purchases
Scenario / Preconditions: Customer history setting is on. Valid non-default customer is selected. API returns no history for this product.
Current App Behavior: System proceeds with current stock or base price.
Question For PM: Should no-history customers always use current price without any prompt?
Suggested Default: Yes, use current price silently.

Real World Example: Regular customer with prior price history
Scenario / Preconditions: Customer history exists for the selected customer and product.
User Action: Cashier chooses Use Current Price in the purchase history modal.
Current App Behavior: System keeps the current stock or base price and continues add-to-cart.
Question For PM: Is choosing current price the right primary action when history exists?
Suggested Default: Yes, current price should remain selectable.

Real World Example: Preferred customer gets old negotiated price
Scenario / Preconditions: Customer history exists for the selected customer and product.
User Action: Cashier chooses a historical price in the purchase history modal.
Current App Behavior: System overrides the selling price with the chosen historical price but keeps the selected stock for tracking.
Question For PM: Should historical price override be allowed while preserving the current selected stock?
Suggested Default: Yes, allow price override but keep stock linkage.

Real World Example: Cashier opens history modal accidentally
Scenario / Preconditions: Purchase history modal is open.
Current App Behavior: Current flow aborts the add-to-cart action entirely.
Question For PM: If cashier cancels customer history modal, should the item still be added at current price, or should add be cancelled?
Suggested Default: Cancel the add to avoid accidental pricing.

Real World Example: Historical price differs from selected stock price
Scenario / Preconditions: Customer selects a historical price that is lower or higher than the stock's current price.
Current App Behavior: Cart line uses historical selling price, but selected stock remains attached and stock_id can still be sent.
Question For PM: Is it valid to keep stock_id from current stock while selling at a historical customer-specific price?
Suggested Default: Yes, if stock controls inventory and price controls billing separately.

Real World Example: Same item from same batch twice
Scenario / Preconditions: Same product is added again with the same selected stock id.
Current App Behavior: System increments quantity on the existing cart row instead of creating a new row.
Question For PM: Is same-product plus same-stock the correct row-merge rule?
Suggested Default: Yes, merge same product and same stock.

Real World Example: Same item from different batches
Scenario / Preconditions: Same product is added again with a different selected stock id.
Current App Behavior: System creates or keeps a separate cart row for the different stock.
Question For PM: Should different stock ids always stay on separate cart rows?
Suggested Default: Yes, keep separate rows.

Real World Example: No-stock fallback item added twice
Scenario / Preconditions: Same product is added again without any selected stock, such as base-price fallback.
Current App Behavior: System merges rows when both cart lines have no selected stock.
Question For PM: Should no-stock base-price lines merge together?
Suggested Default: Yes, merge if product and no-stock context match.

Real World Example: Cashier manually types custom price in Add Item
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock-enabled flow is used, and cashier enters a custom price before adding.
Current App Behavior: System carries the custom price through stock selection flow and adds the item with that explicit price.
Question For PM: Should manual custom price always win over stock price in Add Item flow?
Suggested Default: Yes, if cashier has permission to override price.

Real World Example: Cashier re-adds same item after manual override
Scenario / Preconditions: Item already exists in cart with a custom price. Cashier adds same product and same stock again without giving a new explicit price.
Current App Behavior: System preserves the existing custom price on that cart row.
Question For PM: Should existing custom price remain sticky for repeat adds of the same product and stock?
Suggested Default: Yes, preserve until cashier changes it.

Real World Example: Confirmed order with selected stock
Scenario / Preconditions: Cart line has a selected stock.
Current App Behavior: System includes stock_id in the order payload.
Question For PM: Should selected stock always be sent to API when available?
Suggested Default: Yes, send stock_id for stock-aware orders.

Real World Example: Confirmed order from base-price fallback
Scenario / Preconditions: Cart line has no selected stock because no stock was chosen or none was available.
Current App Behavior: System sends no stock_id or sends null for that line.
Question For PM: Should orders created through fallback selling be allowed to go to API without stock_id?
Suggested Default: Yes only if backend supports non-stock sale lines; otherwise block with warning.

Real World Example: Stock row missing selling price
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock-enabled flow selects a stock row whose price is null or empty.
Current App Behavior: Current flow can end up passing an explicit 0 price to cart in some paths.
Question For PM: If selected stock has no price, should the app fall back to product base price, block sale, or allow 0?
Suggested Default: Never allow silent 0 price; either fall back to product price or block sale.

Real World Example: Stock row missing MRP
Scenario / Preconditions: Stock-enabled flow selects a stock row whose MRP is null or empty.
Current App Behavior: Current flow can end up passing an explicit 0 MRP to cart in some paths.
Question For PM: If selected stock has no MRP, should the app fall back to product MRP, allow blank MRP, or block sale?
Suggested Default: Fall back to product MRP if available.

Real World Example: Normal in-stock sale
Scenario / Preconditions: Selected stock has enough quantity for the requested cart quantity.
Current App Behavior: Stock reduces normally and cart quantity matches stock deducted.
Question For PM: Is standard exact deduction the correct baseline behavior?
Suggested Default: Yes, deduct exactly when stock is sufficient.

Real World Example: Requested sale exceeds available stock
Scenario / Preconditions: Selected stock has less quantity than requested.
User Action: Cashier adds a quantity larger than available stock.
Current App Behavior: Stock is clamped at 0, sale continues, and cart quantity may be greater than actual stock deducted.
Question For PM: Should overselling be allowed when requested quantity exceeds available stock?
Suggested Default: Usually block or warn and cap sale to available quantity.

Real World Example: Cart line increment pushes stock below zero
Scenario / Preconditions: Item already in cart. Additional increment would make selected stock negative.
Current App Behavior: Stock deduction is clamped at 0, but cart quantity still increases and stockDeducted tracks only what was actually deducted.
Question For PM: When increment would oversell, should quantity increase be blocked, capped, or allowed with warning?
Suggested Default: Block or cap the increment to available stock.

Real World Example: Grouped row selected from combined stocks
Scenario / Preconditions: Cashier chooses a grouped pricing row with combined total quantity from multiple raw stock rows.
User Action: Cashier adds a quantity against that grouped row.
Current App Behavior: UI treats the group as one representative stock with total quantity, but underlying deduction across raw rows is not fully distributed.
Question For PM: If grouped rows stay selectable, how should actual quantity deduction be distributed across the underlying stock rows?
Suggested Default: Use FIFO or FEFO across original rows, not one representative row.
